jobs.title: Sr. Manager/Director FP&A
jobs.description:
ABOUT LUMILENS

At Lumilens we are building the critical photonics infrastructure that powers tomorrow’s AI supercomputing. From chip-to-chip optical interconnects to scalable photonic engines, Lumilens is unlocking a new era of computing - faster, cooler, and massively more efficient. 
 
We’re a well-funded startup backed by Mayfield and led by veterans who’ve built and scaled some of the most transformative technologies in the industry. At Lumilens, we’re developing high-speed photonics products purpose-built to power the future of AI infrastructure and high-performance computing. 
 
This isn’t incremental innovation, it’s a ground-floor opportunity to rethink the optical layer from the silicon up. You’ll work alongside a team of world-class engineers solving some of the hardest challenges in scaling optical systems. Every line of code, every design decision, every breakthrough you help deliver will shape the infrastructure of tomorrow. 
 
If you're looking for mission, momentum, and the chance to make an outsized impact, jump on the rocket ship. We’re just getting started.

The Role

This role is at the core of Lumilens’ global FP&A delivery from Bangalore, partnering closely with R&D and business leaders to drive financial planning, business partnership, and decision support. As a member of the India Leadership team, this leader will also collectively act as country controller for the India entity, helping build financial discipline, scalable planning processes, and strong operating visibility in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.

Key Responsibilities

 - Own the annual operating plan, quarterly forecasts, and monthly variance analysis for the assigned SBU or function.

 - Partner with business leaders to drive financial discipline, evaluate investments, and track operational KPIs.

 - Build driver-based financial models across revenue, gross margin, operating expenses, and capital expenditures.

 - Lead pricing analysis, customer and product profitability reviews, and unit economics assessments.

 - Drive India R&D expense planning, tracking, and project-level variance management.

 - Act as country controller for the India entity, including support for statutory close, audit, tax filings, and transfer pricing.

 - Support board reporting, investor relations materials, and earnings preparation in support of a US listing.

 - Drive scenario planning, sensitivity analysis, and strategic financial reviews to support key business decisions.

 - Coach analysts and mentor junior team members while helping build a strong finance organization in India.

Required Qualifications

 - CPA, CFA, or MBA required.

 - 10–15 years of FP&A or strategic finance experience.

 - Technology industry FP&A or strategic finance experience, or an engineering degree combined with an MBA.

 - Ability to operate effectively in a startup environment with ambiguity and limited structure, including building processes from scratch without established playbooks.

 - Strong financial modeling, scenario analysis, and business partnering capabilities.

 - Proven ability to influence senior business leaders through data-driven insights and sound financial judgment.

 - Advanced financial modeling skills and comfort working with large datasets.

Preferred Qualifications

 - Experience in technology, hardware, semiconductor, or FMCG industries.

 - Manufacturing cost accounting exposure.

 - A track record of building and developing finance teams and processes from scratch.

 - US MNC experience as a controller or senior finance leader within a US-headquartered multinational.

What We Offer

 - A highly visible leadership role with the opportunity to shape financial and operational decisions in a fast-scaling deep-tech manufacturing environment.

 - The chance to work at the intersection of finance, operations, and advanced photonics technology—where your analysis directly influences investment, margin, and scale.

 - Competitive compensation commensurate with experience, along with comprehensive health benefits.

 - Meaningful exposure to cross-functional and global leadership teams across Singapore, Thailand, Canada, and the United States.

 - Professional growth and development opportunities, including the ability to build processes, strengthen systems, and help define the next chapter of operations finance at Lumilens.

 - A collaborative, ambitious environment where experienced operators can make an outsized impact and help build something category-defining from the ground up.



*Lumilens is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to race, color, religion, gender, identity, orientation, veteran status, disability, or any other legally protected status.

jobs.title: Senior Program Manager
jobs.description:
SENIOR PROGRAM MANAGER – NPI

About Lumilens

 

At Lumilens, we are building critical photonics infrastructure powering tomorrow’s AI supercomputing. From chip-to-chip optical interconnects to scalable photonic engines, Lumilens is unlocking a new era of computing—faster, cooler, and massively more efficient. Join our collaborative team to shape the future of high-speed optical connectivity.

 

Position Overview

 

We are seeking an experienced Senior Program Manager specializing in New Product Introduction (NPI). The ideal candidate will have over 15 years of experience in the NPI domain, preferably within the switching and networking industry. This leader will demonstrate proven expertise managing programs from early prototyping through pilot manufacturing, with solid exposure to hardware development fundamentals and manufacturing processes.

 

Responsibilities

 

 - Lead complex NPI programs from concept through prototyping and into pilot manufacturing

 - Manage program end-to-end, wall-to-wall, ensuring all phases from initiation to closure are delivered successfully

 - Work extensively with cross-functional teams spread across geographies to ensure alignment and timely delivery

 - Collaborate with engineering, operations, and manufacturing teams to ensure milestones are achieved on schedule

 - Drive planning and execution of early hardware prototyping and transition to scalable manufacturing

 - Manage program risk, develop mitigation plans, and communicate status to stakeholders

 - Ensure robust design transfer processes and readiness for manufacturing

 - Maintain detailed documentation and program tracking tools

 - Champion continuous improvement in program management practices

 

Required Qualifications

 

 - More than 15 years of program management experience in the NPI space, preferably in switching and networking domains

 - Demonstrated proficiency in managing programs end-to-end, wall-to-wall, across all project phases

 - Proven experience working with teams distributed across different global geographies

 - Excellent track record of leading programs from prototyping through pilot manufacturing

 - Strong understanding of hardware design, development processes, and manufacturing fundamentals

 - Proficiency in project management tools, methodologies, and communication

 - Collaborative mindset with strong organizational, analytical, and leadership skills

 - Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Engineering or a related field

 

Why Join Lumilens?

 

 - Work at the forefront of AI, networking, and optical semiconductor technology

 - Collaborative and innovative environment

 - Opportunities for career growth

 - Competitive salary and comprehensive benefits package

 

Lumilens is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, or any other protected characteristic.

jobs.title: General Manager, Singapore
jobs.description:
ABOUT LUMILENS

At Lumilens we are building the critical photonics infrastructure that powers tomorrow’s AI supercomputing. From chip-to-chip optical interconnects to scalable photonic engines, Lumilens is unlocking a new era of computing - faster, cooler, and massively more efficient.

We’re a well-funded startup backed by Mayfield and led by veterans who’ve built and scaled some of the most transformative technologies in the industry. At Lumilens, we’re developing high-speed photonics products purpose-built to power the future of AI infrastructure and high-performance computing.

This isn’t incremental innovation, it’s a ground-floor opportunity to rethink the optical layer from the silicon up. You’ll work alongside a team of world-class engineers solving some of the hardest challenges in scaling optical systems. Every line of code, every design decision, every breakthrough you help deliver will shape the infrastructure of tomorrow.

If you're looking for mission, momentum, and the chance to make an outsized impact, jump on the rocket ship. We’re just getting started.



POSITION OVERVIEW

We are seeking a seasoned General Manager to lead end-to end operational execution as the company scales its next generation optical transceiver and photonics products from NPI into high volume global manufacturing.

As GM you will serve as the single-threaded owner for delivery, cost, quality, and capacity across Lumilens’ manufacturing ecosystem. You’ll work closely with OEM partners, critical component suppliers, and internal engineering and planning teams. This role requires a rare blend of technical depth, operational rigor, supplier leadership, and strategic judgment to translate innovation into reliable, scalable and world-class production.



DUTIES / RESPONSIBILITIES

1. Own end-to-end operational execution for Lumilens’ product portfolio (800G / 1.6T optical modules and beyond), with full accountability for on-time delivery, cost, quality, and scalable ramp-up.

2. Serve as the ultimate escalation authority for all production, yield, capacity, quality, and supplier-related issues to ensure rapid resolution

3. Translate customer demand and revenue targets into executable build plans, capacity commitments, and supply strategies.

4. Lead and govern Lumilens’ global manufacturing ecosystem, including EMS/ODM partners, OSATs, fabs, and critical sub-tier suppliers.

5. Drive capacity planning, ramp readiness, and risk mitigation across multiple sites.

6. Negotiate and manage commercial agreements, including pricing, capacity reservations, long-term supply commitments, and cost-down initiatives with key vendors.

7. Establish and maintain robust dual-sourcing strategies, second-source qualifications, and supplier contingency plans to ensure supply continuity.

8. Own COGS performance, BOM cost reductions, PPV tracking, and long-term cost-down roadmaps.

9. Act as an operational partner to Product and Hardware Engineering teams, to ensure seamless alignment between design intent and manufacturing execution.

10. Embed design-for-manufacturability (DFM/DFX) principles early in the NPI lifecycle to enable scalable, high-yield production.

11. Build scalable operating cadence, including weekly build reviews, QBRs with suppliers, and executive dashboards.

12. Implement and mature processes for demand planning, S&OP, supplier scorecards, and quality management.

13. Build, mentor, and lead a high-performing team across operations, supply chain, planning, and quality.

14. Create clarity of ownership, accountability, and decision rights across functions.



QUALIFICATIONS:

 - Progressive leadership experience in operations, manufacturing, or supply chain roles within hardware, deep-tech, or advanced electronics environments.

 - Proven track record of scaling products from NPI through high-volume manufacturing, including ownership of yield, quality, cost, and delivery.

 - Strong technical foundation in optics, semiconductors, electronics manufacturing, or closely related industries; experience with optical transceivers, data-centre hardware, or high-speed networking products is preferred

 - Bachelor’s degree or advanced technical degree/ MBA in electrical engineering, Industrial Engineering, Physics, or a related field.

 - Deep hands-on expertise in manufacturing process development, yield analysis, root-cause problem solving, and implementation of corrective actions.

 - Strong commercial acumen, with experience negotiating pricing, capacity commitments, long-term supply agreements, and cost-reduction initiatives.

 - In-depth knowledge of quality management systems (QMS), reliability testing, and quality standards applicable to high-volume electronics and optics manufacturing.

 - Experience working across Asia-based manufacturing hubs, including Taiwan, Thailand, China, and Vietnam. Experience working in Singapore will be an advantage.

 - Resourceful and analytical problem-solver, capable of managing multiple concurrent programs and priorities in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment.

 - Proven ability to operate effectively within geographically distributed, cross-functional teams, partnering closely with engineering, quality, finance, and commercial functions.

 - Strong English communication skills, both written and verbal, with the ability to present to senior stakeholders and mentor and develop teams.

 - Willingness and ability to travel internationally as required.



Equal Employment Opportunity

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, religious creed, sex, national origin, ancestry, age, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, military or veteran status, marital status, pregnancy, gender, gender expression, gender identity, sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable local laws and regulations.

POSITION OVERVIEW

We are seeking a Strategic Sourcing Manager to join our rapidly growing team. This role is critical in building and scaling a resilient, high-performance supplier network to support our next-generation photonics products.

You will own supplier strategy, sourcing, commercial negotiations, and supply continuity across key categories including silicon photonics, advanced packaging, and optical components. The ideal candidate will build strong supplier relationships, negotiate pricing and terms, and work cross-functionally with engineering, operations, and manufacturing partners to align sourcing decisions with product development and production goals. This is a highly visible role with direct impact on cost, quality, scalability, and time-to-market.



What You'll Do

 - Develop and execute strategic sourcing plans aligned with product roadmaps and company growth objectives

 - Identify, qualify, onboard, and manage key suppliers across component vendors, contract manufacturers, and strategic manufacturing partners

 - Lead supplier negotiations across pricing, lead times, capacity, quality, and commercial terms. Negotiate and execute master supply agreements and other critical commercial agreements, including Statement of Work (SOW), development agreements, NDAs, etc.

 - Drive cost optimization initiatives through early design engagement, market intelligence, should-cost modeling, supplier process improvement, and long-term supply agreements.

 - Ensure supply continuity and mitigate risk through multi-sourcing, supplier performance management, and contingency planning

 - Partner with cross functional teams to drive supplier selection process (own RFx), support component and module qualification during NPI programs and enable smooth transitions to high-volume manufacturing

 - Collaborate with operations and manufacturing partners to align demand, capacity, and delivery commitments

 - Develop and drive supplier performance against KPIs including cost, quality, delivery, responsiveness, capacity and innovation

 - Act as the primary escalation path for his/her respective commodity.



Key Qualifications

 - Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Engineering, Business, or related field

 - 10+ years of experience in strategic sourcing, supplier management, or supply chain management within semiconductor, photonics, or high-tech industries

 - Strong experience working with global suppliers including contract manufacturers, specialty component vendors, and strategic manufacturing partners

 - Experience in optical technologies and demonstrated experience with deployment of manufacturing processes

 - Proven track record supporting NPI to HVM transitions in complex hardware environments and with contract manufacturers

 - Deep understanding of strategic sourcing fundamentals including cost modeling, supplier negotiations, contract terms, and risk management

 - Experience working embedding with hardware engineering throughout product development process

 - Ability to operate cross-functionally and influence stakeholders across engineering, product management, operations, and finance

 - Actively participate in solving operational challenges to keep product schedules on track

 - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with a data-driven mindset

 - Experience in fast-paced, high-growth environments

Preferred Skills

 - Experience in silicon photonics, optical transceivers, or advanced packaging

 - Familiarity with ERP/MRP systems and supply chain analytics tools

 - Experience building supply chains from early-stage to scale

 - Knowledge of global trade, logistics, and compliance considerations

Why Join Us?

● Competitive salary commensurate with experience 
● Comprehensive benefits package including health insurance 
● Professional development opportunities and certification support 
● Access to cutting-edge photonics and advanced manufacturing technologies 
● Collaborative work environment with cross-functional teams solving complex challenges

jobs.title: Sourcing Manager (Foundry & OSAT)
jobs.description:
CORE RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Supplier Strategy & Selection: Work with management on the long-term global sourcing strategies and identify, evaluate, and select top-tier foundry and OSAT partners.

 - Capacity & Demand Planning: Negotiate and secure capacity & CT of wafer, assembly, and test services to meet product roadmaps and revenue goals.

 - Cost Optimization: Lead "should-cost" analysis, drive competitive RFQs (Request for Quotations), pricing benchmarking and negotiate pricing and contracts to achieve cost reduction targets.

 - Manufacturing Service Agreement (MSA): Participate in the drafting of MSA. Review the adequacy of MSA to ensure manufacturing delivery commitment and financial obligation by the suppliers. Enforce the T&C of MSA.

 - Others: Company’s advocate to escalate and resolve commercial & delivery issues. Participate in QBR with the suppliers and drive commercial improvements.

 - Cross-Functional Alignment: Work closely with engineering, supply chain, and business units to align sourcing with new product development (NPD).




PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS & EXPERIENCE

 - Education: Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Science, Supply Chain Management, or Finance.

 - Experience: 5-10+ years of procurement or supply chain management experience specifically within the semiconductor, foundry, and/or OSAT industry.

 - Technical Knowledge: Understanding of wafer fabrication processes, advanced packaging (e.g., WLP, 2.5D/3D), and testing, or semiconductor planning/production control experience, an added advantage.

 - Core Skills: Exceptional commercial acumen, high-level contract negotiation abilities, data-driven analytical & reporting skills.

 - Language/Travel: Fluency in English and Mandarin (added advantage) to communicate with stakeholders from Mandarin speaking regions, with international travel capabilities.

jobs.title: Supply Chain Planning Manager (Production)
jobs.description:
About LUMILENS

At Lumilens, we’re developing high-speed photonics products purpose-built to power the future of AI infrastructure and high-performance computing.

 

This isn’t incremental innovation, it’s a ground-floor opportunity to rethink the optical layer from the silicon up. You’ll work alongside a team of world-class engineers solving some of the hardest challenges in scaling optical systems. If you're looking for mission, momentum, and the chance to make an outsized impact, jump on the rocket ship. We’re just getting started.

 

Role Overview

We are seeking an experienced Supply Chain Planning Manager to own end-to-end supply chain execution for volume production, ensuring materials, capacity, and inventory are aligned with production building schedules and ramp requirements. This role is responsible for MRP-driven material planning, CM build plan management, inventory optimization, and ongoing supplier risk management to keep production running reliably on a scale.

 

Key Responsibilities

Supply Chain Planning

 - Translate production forecasts and build plans into MRP, procurement plans, and supplier commitments.

 - Monitor and optimize inventory levels, safety stock, and material consumption to minimize wastage while protecting build continuity.

Execution

 - Lead supply chain readiness across production builds at CM partners.

 - Coordinate build schedules, material availability, and logistics with CM partners and suppliers to support ongoing production volume.

 - Support engineering change management for production-phase design revisions, ensuring supply chain plans stay aligned.

 - Manage the transition from NPI/pilot builds into steady-state production ramp, in coordination with NPI supply chain and engineering teams.

Supplier & Manufacturing Coordination

 - Develop and manage the production build plan at CM partners, aligned with demand and business requirements.

 - Monitor supplier lead times, capacity constraints, and delivery commitments at production volume.

 - Work with procurement to secure ongoing material supply and manufacturing capacity as volumes scale.

Risk Management

 - Identify potential material shortages, supply disruptions, or single-source risks affecting production continuity.

 - Maintain visibility of critical-path components and long-lead items across the production supply base.

Analytics & Reporting

 - Track key supply chain metrics including forecast accuracy, inventory turns, and on-time material availability for production.

 - Provide regular updates on production supply readiness and risks to cross-functional leadership.

 

Qualifications

 - Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Materials Science, Supply Chain, or a related field.

 - 5+ years of experience in supply chain planning, material planning, or MRP execution, ideally in electronics, semiconductor, or hardware manufacturing.

 - Proven track record managing material and supply plans across multiple sites/regions coordinating with suppliers and contract manufacturing (CM) partners to keep build schedules on track.

 - Hands-on experience with an ERP/MRP system (SAP, Oracle, NetSuite, or similar) and strong Excel/data skills.

 - Excellent analytical, forecasting, and cross-functional stakeholder management skill

 - Experience with inventory optimization is a strong plus.

jobs.description:
About LUMILENS

At Lumilens we are building the critical photonics infrastructure that powers tomorrow’s AI supercomputing. From chip-to-chip optical interconnects to scalable photonic engines, Lumilens is unlocking a new era of computing - faster, cooler, and massively more efficient.

You’ll work alongside a team of world-class engineers solving some of the hardest challenges in scaling optical systems. If you're looking for mission, momentum, and the chance to make an outsized impact, jump on the rocket ship. We’re just getting started.



Role Overview

We are seeking an experienced Supply Chain Manager to lead sourcing strategy and end-to-end supply chain management for optical and photonic components — including lasers, photonic integrated circuits (PICs), photodetectors (PDs), fiber array units (FAUs), This role owns supplier identification, qualification, negotiation, and relationship management across a global supply base, while also ensuring supplier capacity, lead times, and allocations stay aligned with build schedules and ramp requirements. The ideal candidate combines strong sourcing/negotiation expertise with supply chain planning fluency and enough technical grounding in optics/photonics to evaluate supplier capability and de-risk single-source dependencies.



Key Responsibilities

Supply Chain Planning & Allocation

 - Translate plans and forecasts into supplier capacity requirements and allocation requests for sourced commodities.

 - Monitor supplier lead times, allocation cycles, and delivery commitments, and flag gaps against build schedules early.

 - Coordinate with planning and production teams to align supplier capacity and delivery commitments with prototype, pilot, and production build schedules.

 - Develop and manage supply plans, balancing demand forecasts, inventory targets, and manufacturing capabilities across global partners

 - Establish planning processes, metrics, and governance to enable consistent, data-driven decision making

 - Lead continuous improvement initiatives to enhance supply chain agility, efficiency, a responsiveness in a fast-scale environment

Supplier Identification & Qualification

 - Lead supplier qualification activities in partnership with engineering and quality teams (technical audits, sample evaluation, process capability review).

 - Assess supplier financial health, manufacturing capacity, and technology roadmap alignment.

 - Support commercial negotiations for pricing, capacity commitments, and supply agreements with optics/photonics suppliers

 - Partner with engineering and product teams to translate technology roadmaps into sourcing plans, well ahead of production needs.

 - Own cost-reduction roadmaps for key commodities, tracking savings against targets.



Supply Risk Management

 - Maintain visibility of long-lead and critical-path optical components across the supply base.

 - Proactively identify and mitigate supply risks: allocation constraints, single-source exposure, geopolitical/export-control exposure, and capacity shortfalls.

 - Build contingency and dual-source plans for critical components identified as at-risk.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

 - Partner cross-functionally with engineering, operations, and program management to translate product requirements into scalable supply chain strategies

 - Work closely with engineering on component specifications, alternate part qualification, and second-source enablement.

 - Support contract manufacturing (CM) partners with supplier introductions and component allocation, where components are consigned or CM-managed.

Analytics & Reporting

 - Track supplier performance: on-time delivery, quality (PPM/yield), cost trends, and capacity utilization.

 - Maintain a sourcing and supply roadmap and risk dashboard for optics/photonics commodities, reporting regularly to supply chain and engineering leadership.



Qualifications

jobs.title: Strategic Sourcing Manager
jobs.description:
About Lumilens

At Lumilens we are building the critical photonics infrastructure that powers tomorrow’s AI supercomputing. From chip-to-chip optical interconnects to scalable photonic engines, Lumilens is unlocking a new era of computing faster, cooler, and massively more efficient.

We’re a well-funded startup backed by Mayfield and led by veterans who’ve built and scaled some of the most transformative technologies in the industry. This isn’t incremental innovation, it’s a ground-floor opportunity to rethink the optical layer from the silicon up. You’ll work alongside a team of world-class engineers solving some of the hardest challenges in optics, systems, and scale. Every decision you make will directly influence how we build, source, and deliver the infrastructure of tomorrow.

If you're looking for mission, momentum, and the chance to make an outsized impact, jump on the rocket ship. We’re just getting started.

Position Overview

We are seeking a Strategic Sourcing Manager to join our rapidly growing team. This role is critical in building and scaling a resilient, high-performance supplier network to support our next-generation photonics products.

You will own supplier strategy, sourcing, commercial negotiations, and supply continuity across key categories including silicon photonics, advanced packaging, and optical components. The ideal candidate will build strong supplier relationships, negotiate pricing and terms, and work cross-functionally with engineering, operations, and manufacturing partners to align sourcing decisions with product development and production goals. This is a highly visible role with direct impact on cost, quality, scalability, and time-to-market.

What You'll Do


 - Develop and execute strategic sourcing plans aligned with product roadmaps and company growth objectives

 - Identify, qualify, onboard, and manage key suppliers across component vendors, contract manufacturers, and strategic manufacturing partners

 - Lead supplier negotiations across pricing, lead times, capacity, quality, and commercial terms. Negotiate and execute master supply agreements and other critical commercial agreements, including Statement of Work (SOW), development agreements, NDAs, etc. 

 - Drive cost optimization initiatives through early design engagement, market intelligence, should-cost modeling, supplier process improvement, and long-term supply agreements. 

 - Ensure supply continuity and mitigate risk through multi-sourcing, supplier performance management, and contingency planning

 - Partner with cross functional teams to drive supplier selection process (own RFx), support component and module qualification during NPI programs and enable smooth transitions to high-volume manufacturing

 - Collaborate with operations and manufacturing partners to align demand, capacity, and delivery commitments

 - Develop and drive supplier performance against KPIs including cost, quality, delivery, responsiveness, capacity and innovation

 - Act as the primary escalation path for his/her respective commodity. 

Key Qualifications


 - Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Engineering, Business, or related field

 - 10+ years of experience in strategic sourcing, supplier management, or supply chain management within semiconductor, photonics, or high-tech industries

 - Strong experience working with global suppliers including contract manufacturers, specialty component vendors, and strategic manufacturing partners

 - Experience in optical technologies and demonstrated experience with deployment of manufacturing processes

 - Proven track record supporting NPI to HVM transitions in complex hardware environments and with contract manufacturers

 - Deep understanding of strategic sourcing fundamentals including cost modeling, supplier negotiations, contract terms, and risk management

 - Experience working embedding with hardware engineering throughout product development process

 - Ability to operate cross-functionally and influence stakeholders across engineering, product management, operations, and finance

 - Actively participate in solving operational challenges to keep product schedules on track

 - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with a data-driven mindset

 - Experience in fast-paced, high-growth environments

Preferred Skills


 - Experience in silicon photonics, optical transceivers, or advanced packaging

 - Familiarity with ERP/MRP systems and supply chain analytics tools

 - Experience building supply chains from early-stage to scale

 - Knowledge of global trade, logistics, and compliance considerations

Why Join Us?


 - Competitive salary commensurate with experience

 - Comprehensive benefits package including health insurance

 - Professional development opportunities and certification support

 - Access to cutting-edge photonics and advanced manufacturing technologies

 - Collaborative work environment with cross-functional teams solving complex challenges

Lumilens is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to race, color, religion, gender, identity, orientation, veteran status, disability, or any other legally protected status.

jobs.title: Capital Equipment Sourcing & Procurement Director
jobs.description:
We are seeking an experienced Director of Capital Equipment Sourcing & Procurement to lead the strategy, negotiation, and execution of all capital equipment purchases across the organization. This is a high-impact leadership role responsible for millions of dollars in annual capital spend, supplier relationships, and the processes that ensure equipment is delivered on time, at the right cost, and to the right specification.

You will partner closely with Engineering, Operations, Finance, and Facilities to translate technical requirements into sourcing strategies, manage a portfolio of equipment vendors, and drive cost savings and risk reduction across the capital equipment lifecycle — from specification through installation and warranty support.




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

• Sourcing Strategy: Develop and execute category strategies for capital equipment (e.g., production/manufacturing equipment, lab/test equipment, tooling) aligned with business growth plans and capital budgets.

• Supplier Management: Identify, qualify, and manage a global supplier base; negotiate pricing, terms, warranties, and service agreements; build long-term strategic partnerships with key OEMs and equipment vendors.

• Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work directly with Engineering and Operations teams to define technical specifications, evaluate vendor proposals, and ensure equipment selections meet performance, quality, and compliance requirements.

• Contract Negotiation: Lead complex negotiations for capital equipment purchases, including pricing, payment terms, delivery schedules, installation/commissioning support, spare parts, and service level agreements.

• Capital Budget Ownership: Partner with Finance to build, track, and manage the capital equipment budget; provide forecasting, spend analysis, and ROI justification for major purchases.

• Risk & Compliance: Manage supply risk (single-source exposure, lead times, geopolitical/tariff exposure) and ensure procurement activities comply with company policy, export controls, and relevant regulatory requirements.

• Process & Systems: Build and continuously improve procurement processes, approval workflows, and sourcing playbooks; leverage procurement/ERP systems for visibility and reporting.

• Team Leadership: Hire, mentor, and manage a team of buyers/sourcing specialists as the function scales (if applicable).

• Vendor Performance: Establish KPIs and scorecards to track supplier performance on cost, quality, delivery, and after-sales support; drive corrective actions where needed.

• Cost Savings: Identify and deliver measurable cost reduction, cost avoidance, and total-cost-of-ownership improvements across the capital equipment portfolio.




QUALIFICATIONS

Required

• Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Supply Chain Management, Business, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience).

• 10+ years of progressive experience in procurement, strategic sourcing, or supply chain management, with at least 3–5 years focused specifically on capital equipment.

• Proven track record negotiating large, complex capital equipment contracts.

• Strong technical fluency — able to read equipment specifications and engage credibly with engineering teams on technical trade-offs.

• Deep understanding of the capital equipment lifecycle: RFQ/RFP processes, vendor qualification, contract structuring, installation/commissioning, and warranty management.

• Excellent negotiation, communication, and stakeholder management skills across all levels of the organization.

• Experience managing capital budgets and building cost justification/ROI models.

Preferred

• Experience in semiconductor manufacturing, contract manufacturing, or equipment engineering.

• Experience sourcing internationally and managing supplier relationships across regions.

• Familiarity with import/export regulations, tariffs, and customs processes as they relate to capital equipment.

• People management experience leading a sourcing or buyer team.

jobs.title: Supply Chain Manager
jobs.description:
About LUMILENS

At Lumilens we are building the critical photonics infrastructure that powers tomorrow’s AI supercomputing. From chip-to-chip optical interconnects to scalable photonic engines, Lumilens is unlocking a new era of computing - faster, cooler, and massively more efficient. 

We’re a well-funded startup backed by Mayfield and led by veterans who’ve built and scaled some of the most transformative technologies in the industry. At Lumilens, we’re developing high-speed photonics products purpose-built to power the future of AI infrastructure and high-performance computing. 

This isn’t incremental innovation, it’s a ground-floor opportunity to rethink the optical layer from the silicon up. You’ll work alongside a team of world-class engineers solving some of the hardest challenges in scaling optical systems. If you're looking for mission, momentum, and the chance to make an outsized impact, jump on the rocket ship. We’re just getting started.



Role Overview

We are seeking an experienced Supply Chain Manager to lead sourcing strategy and end-to-end supply chain management for optical and photonic components — including lasers, photonic integrated circuits (PICs), photodetectors (PDs), fiber array units (FAUs), This role owns supplier identification, qualification, negotiation, and relationship management across a global supply base, while also ensuring supplier capacity, lead times, and allocations stay aligned with build schedules and ramp requirements. The ideal candidate combines strong sourcing/negotiation expertise with supply chain planning fluency and enough technical grounding in optics/photonics to evaluate supplier capability and de-risk single-source dependencies.



Key Responsibilities

Supply Chain Planning & Allocation

 - Translate plans and forecasts into supplier capacity requirements and allocation requests for sourced commodities.

 - Monitor supplier lead times, allocation cycles, and delivery commitments, and flag gaps against build schedules early.

 - Coordinate with planning and production teams to align supplier capacity and delivery commitments with prototype, pilot, and production build schedules.

 - Develop and manage supply plans, balancing demand forecasts, inventory targets, and manufacturing capabilities across global partners

 - Establish planning processes, metrics, and governance to enable consistent, data-driven decision making

 - Lead continuous improvement initiatives to enhance supply chain agility, efficiency, a responsiveness in a fast-scale environment

Supplier Identification & Qualification

 - Lead supplier qualification activities in partnership with engineering and quality teams (technical audits, sample evaluation, process capability review).

 - Assess supplier financial health, manufacturing capacity, and technology roadmap alignment.

 - Support commercial negotiations for pricing, capacity commitments, and supply agreements with optics/photonics suppliers

 - Partner with engineering and product teams to translate technology roadmaps into sourcing plans, well ahead of production needs.

 - Own cost-reduction roadmaps for key commodities, tracking savings against targets.



Supply Risk Management

 - Maintain visibility of long-lead and critical-path optical components across the supply base.

 - Proactively identify and mitigate supply risks: allocation constraints, single-source exposure, geopolitical/export-control exposure, and capacity shortfalls.

 - Build contingency and dual-source plans for critical components identified as at-risk.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

 - Partner cross-functionally with engineering, operations, and program management to translate product requirements into scalable supply chain strategies

 - Work closely with engineering on component specifications, alternate part qualification, and second-source enablement.

 - Support contract manufacturing (CM) partners with supplier introductions and component allocation, where components are consigned or CM-managed.

Analytics & Reporting

 - Track supplier performance: on-time delivery, quality (PPM/yield), cost trends, and capacity utilization.

 - Maintain a sourcing and supply roadmap and risk dashboard for optics/photonics commodities, reporting regularly to supply chain and engineering leadership.



Qualifications

 - Bachelor’s degree in engineering, Materials Science, Supply Chain, or related field

 - 5+ years of sourcing/procurement and supply chain experience

 - Proven track record negotiating supply agreements and managing supplier relationships across Asia and other global regions.

 - Excellent analytical and cross-functional stakeholder management skills.
